claims.text: DFT calculations can effectively control phase evolution in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEAs.
DFT can predict the formation energies of constituent phases in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEAs.
DFT can predict the stability of constituent phases in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEAs.
The initial Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEA is in a disordered FCC phase.
The proposed calculations use a plane-wave basis set and the PBE exchange-correlation functional.
The calculations are performed at 0 K and 1 atm.
Calculations at 0 K and 1 atm represent idealized alloy-design conditions and minimize effects from thermal vibrations and pressure.
The formation energy of constituent phases is the structural mediator linking DFT calculations to phase evolution.
Ab initio calculations obtain electronic structure by solving the Schrödinger equation.
Predicted phase stability and formation energies allow optimal alloy compositions to be identified.
Predicted phase stability and formation energies allow processing conditions that minimize secondary-phase formation to be identified.
DFT-guided optimization will reduce secondary phases formed during solidification by 20% ± 10% relative to conventional processing.
The hypothesis applies to compositions varying by no more than 10 at.% from the unspecified baseline composition.
A maximum variation of 10 at.% corresponds to the expected solid-solubility range of the constituent elements.
The predicted reduction has an uncertainty of ±10% because of DFT limitations and finite-temperature and pressure effects in actual processing.

contradictions.description: The predicted 20% ± 10% reduction permits reductions as low as 10%, while the nominal falsification threshold requires at least a 15% ± 5% reduction. Thus, some outcomes can fall within the stated prediction interval yet also satisfy the stated falsification condition.
